headline: This law updates how the government prepares for handing presidential power from one administration to the next.
what_it_does: The law requires the President to set up a transition coordinating council and an agency transition directors council, starting at least six months before an election. The General Services Administration must name a senior career official as Federal Transition Coordinator to lead planning across agencies and work with eligible candidates' transition teams. Agencies must name senior career employees to oversee transition work, and the coordinator must negotiate access rules for incoming transition staff. The law also requires several reports to Congress on transition preparation, presidential records funding, political appointees moving into civil service jobs, late-term regulations, and threats during a transition.

who_it_affects.how: They gain a formal process, including a memorandum of understanding, that sets the terms for access to agency employees, facilities, and documents.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies and their senior career employees
who_it_affects.how: Each agency must designate a senior career employee to oversee transition work and meet new planning and reporting requirements.

who_it_affects.group: Political appointees seeking nonpolitical civil service jobs
who_it_affects.how: Agency requests to place political or former political appointees in nonpolitical civil service positions are reported to Congress.
The President's budget request must include funding for managing and caring for presidential records in the final year of a presidential term.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on March 18, 2016, and some duties start about six months before a presidential election, with certain reports due on set dates.
